current.note: H5/D92: thresholds are the SHIPPED engine's measured values. The shipped default is now hybrid (legacy primary + lattice secondary, D81). Measured, not chosen, and not rounded down: precision 267/270, recall 267/288, ClassRecall:Hyphenation 173/176. D77 applies unchanged from here on - within this measurement base thresholds may only move up. Running --ocr-engine legacy now reports FAIL by design: the gate states that the shipped pipeline beats its fallback.

legacy.note: R5.0d re-measurement (was R4.0c's 12-record measurement: CorrectlyFixed=148, WronglyFixed=0, Deferred=12). Against the 288-record schemaVersion-3 ground truth, legacy now shows real wrong-corrections for the first time: odun-kesmek-glyph-0030 ('olın'->'olan', independently verified correct answer is 'John' - EvidenceOnly confidence, the lowest tier legacy has), odun-kesmek-mixed-0022 ('kol-1 ıı kta', legacy only fixes the inner 'ıı'->'ı' sub-span and leaves the surrounding hyphen/digit, so the occurrence reads 'kol-1 ı kta' - not 'koltukta'; this is the one D65 already flagged as legacy's own defect fixed correctly only by lattice's sibling occurrence), and odun-kesmek-auto-0174 ('zencileri-11in', hyphenation removes the dash but the OCR stage leaves the '11' digits untouched, producing 'zencileri11in'). G1 (D80, 2026-09-15): these measured values are now the gate's current threshold - the gate PASSES against this run.

hybrid.note: H5 re-measurement and the shipped configuration. H4b-1 (RetainedGarbage, D91) turned odun-kesmek-garbage-0001 from a wrong fix into a correct one: 266/4 -> 267/3. The three remaining wrong fixes (glyph-0030 'olin'->'olan' where the verified answer is 'John', mixed-0022, auto-0174) are all inherited from the legacy primary and are X2's subject - hybrid adds none of its own, which is D90's acceptance criterion. These are the values the current gate thresholds are taken from (D92).

lattice.note: R5.0d re-measurement (was R5.0a's 12-record measurement: CorrectlyFixed=149, WronglyFixed=1, Deferred=10, recall 93.12%, gate PASS). Against the 288-record ground truth the gate now FAILS just as sharply as it passed before: recall 58.33% < 92.5%, ClassRecall:Hyphenation 88.64% < 100% - precision stays just above the 98% floor (98.25%) but is now measured on 168 correct fixes instead of 1. This is the headline confirmation of D68/D69's premise: the old 12-record gate never actually exercised the lattice engine's recall gap (D64); it does now. The KAYIP-sourced ground truth (119 records where legacy fixes and lattice does not) explains almost all of the recall drop. G1 (D80, 2026-09-15): against the new 288-record threshold profile, lattice still fails on aggregate Recall and ClassRecall:Hyphenation - this is the expected, correct outcome (Faz 5's target distance), not a regression to fix by lowering the gate.

profile.note: R5.0a: gate is now class-breakdown aware and can run with either OCR engine (--ocr-engine legacy|lattice). Aggregate thresholds and classRecallThresholds were fit to the 160-record schemaVersion-2 ground truth (D64: that ground truth barely touched the OCR engines - 160 records with almost no intersection against the 120 production mutations). Superseded by G1/D80 on 2026-09-15 once the ground truth grew to 288 records (schemaVersion 3, R5.0d) and both engines were re-measured against it: both FAILED the 92.5%/98%/Hyphenation-100% thresholds below (legacy: recall 89.93%, ClassRecall:Hyphenation 96.59%; lattice: recall 58.33%, ClassRecall:Hyphenation 88.64%). Per D77/kural 4.5 this profile's thresholds cannot be lowered to make the new baseline pass - instead a new profile is measured from the new baseline (see current).

G1/D80 profile: thresholds were legacy's measured values because legacy was the shipped default. H5 flipped the default to hybrid, which measures strictly above legacy on both aggregate axes (precision 98.89% > 98.85%, recall 92.71% > 89.93%) and on ClassRecall:Hyphenation (98.30% > 96.59%). D77's ratchet therefore allows - and D92 requires - raising the thresholds to the shipped engine's measured values. Same measurement base (288 records, schemaVersion 3), so this is a ratchet inside the base, not a rebuild: legacy alone no longer clears this gate, which is the intended statement that the shipped pipeline beats its own fallback.
